reasoning_traces.think:
Operator tasks define a formal control system over operational states. Each task \( T_i \) is a predicate \( P_i(R) \) on a database row \( R \), where \( R \in \mathcal{D} \) is the domain of data entities. The system enforces a dualism between verification and execution: \( \text{verify}(T_i) \to \text{repo} \) and \( \text{execute}(T_i) \to \text{DB} \). For \( T_{\text{stale}} \), the predicate \( P_{\text{published}} \land \text{stale} \) triggers a \( \text{state-change} \) \( \sigma_{\text{published}} \to \sigma_{\text{unpublished}} \). The \( \text{dry-run} \) mode \( U_{\text{execute}} = \text{false} \) ensures safety. Failure modes include: 1) \( \text{rename-id} \to \text{audit-mismatch} \); 2) \( \text{agent-session} \to \text{denied} \); 3) \( \text{execute without DB} \to \text{no-op} \).
